content: Perindopril/indapamide is a combination medication available in tablet form. Each tablet contains 2 mg of perindopril tert-butylamine salt and 0.625 mg of indapamide. It is specifically indicated for the treatment of essential hypertension. The recommended dosage is one tablet per day, preferably taken in the morning before a meal. This fixed-dose combination includes an ACE inhibitor (perindopril) and a chlorosulfamoyl diuretic (indapamide), which work together to produce a synergistic antihypertensive effect. The pharmacological benefits stem from the individual properties of each component, as well as their combined action on vascular endothelium, microcirculation in arterioles and capillaries, and the target organs affected by hypertension. For elderly patients, the standard dosage is appropriate. In cases of renal impairment, no dosage adjustment is required if the creatinine clearance (CrCl) is greater than 30 mL/min. However, the medication is contraindicated in patients with a CrCl below 30 mL/min. Absolute contraindications include known hypersensitivity to perindopril, indapamide, or sulfonamides; a history of Quincke's edema (angioedema) associated with prior ACE inhibitor use; severe renal failure; significant liver dysfunction; hypokalemia; pregnancy; and lactation. Relative contraindications involve concurrent use with lithium, potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, or medications that may induce cardiac rhythm disturbances. Potential side effects include fatigue, dizziness, headaches, mood changes, sleep disturbances, muscle cramps, hypotension, allergic reactions, skin rashes, gastrointestinal symptoms, dry cough, and dry mouth. Elderly patients and those with heart failure may be at risk of dehydration. Additionally, alterations in laboratory test results may occur. Special warnings apply to immunosuppressed patients and those undergoing hemodialysis, as there is a risk of anaphylactoid reactions when using polyacrylonitrile membranes. Patients with liver impairment should also exercise caution. Precautions should be taken in individuals with electrolyte imbalances, diabetes, gout, hypotension, strict sodium-free diets, heart failure, renal failure, atherosclerosis, or renal artery stenosis, as well as in elderly patients. Drug interactions to avoid include combinations with lithium, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, antiarrhythmic drugs that may cause torsades de pointes, anesthetic agents, and cytostatic or immunosuppressive medications.
